title: Cinema Seat Allocation
statement:
A cinema has `n` rows numbered `1` to `n`, and every row holds 10 seats numbered `1` to `10`. Each `reservedSeats[i] = [row, seat]` marks one seat that is already taken.

You want to seat as many groups of four people as possible. A group must sit in one row, in exactly one of these blocks of seats:

- seats `2`–`5`
- seats `4`–`7`
- seats `6`–`9`

A block can be given to a group only when none of its four seats is reserved, and no seat may be shared by two groups. Return the largest number of groups that can be seated.
notes:
## Intuition

A row can hold at most two groups, and only as seats `2`–`5` plus `6`–`9`. A row with no reservation always gets those two. So only rows that appear in `reservedSeats` need thought, and there are at most `10^4` of them, even though `n` can be a billion. For one row, gather its reserved seats into a bitmask; each block is then a single `&` test. Trying every subset of blocks per row also works, but the masks make the decision a few comparisons.

## Approach

1. Group the reservations by row in the map `rows`, setting bit `seat` of that row's `mask`.
2. Build three constant masks: `left` (seats 2–5), `middle` (4–7) and `right` (6–9).
3. Every row missing from `rows` is empty, so start `groups` at `2 * (n - rows.size)`.
4. For each reserved row, if both `left` and `right` are free, add 2.
5. Otherwise, if any one of `left`, `right` or `middle` is free, add 1. Two groups cannot use `middle` together with another block, since they overlap.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 3`. Row 1 has seats `{2, 3, 8}`: `left` and `right` are both blocked, but `middle` (4–7) is free, so it adds 1. Row 2 has seat `{6}`: `left` is free, so it adds 1. Row 3 has `{1, 10}`: both `left` and `right` are free, so it adds 2. No row is untouched, so `groups = 0 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m), where m is `reservedSeats.length`: one pass to build the masks and one over the distinct rows.
- Space: O(m) for the map.

## Pitfalls

- Never loop over all `n` rows; `n` reaches `10^9`.
- Seats `1` and `10` block nothing, but their row still lands in `rows`; the masks make that harmless.
- `middle` overlaps both other blocks, so a row never gets `middle` plus another group.
- Count each row once even when it has several reservations; that is why they are merged into one mask.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows` | map from a reserved row to the bitmask of its taken seats |
| `left`, `middle`, `right` | bitmasks of seats 2–5, 4–7 and 6–9 |
| `groups` | number of groups seated so far |
| `mask` | taken seats of the current row |
| `leftFree`, `rightFree` | whether the outer blocks of this row are open |

narration.2: Map each row that has a reservation to a bitmask of its taken seats.
narration.4: Set bit seat in that row's mask, starting from 0 for a new row.
narration.10: Rows with no reservation always fit two groups.
narration.12: Now decide each reserved row from its mask.
narration.13: The left block is usable when none of its bits is set.
narration.14: Same test for the right block.
narration.15: Both outer blocks are open: the row fits two groups.
narration.17: Otherwise a single open block of any kind still fits one group.
narration.21: Return the total across all rows.
